statement: In a class of 30 children, two fifths walk to school and one third come by bus. The rest come by car. How many children come by car?

choices.misconception: I worked out how many children walk and stopped there.
I took one fifth of 30 for the walkers instead of two fifths.
I took away the walkers but forgot the children who come by bus.
I took away the bus children but forgot the walkers.

hints: Find how many children walk and how many take the bus.
A fraction of 30 is found by dividing 30 into equal parts and taking the right number of them. Work out the walkers and the bus children separately, then take both groups away from 30.
One fifth of 30 is 6, so two fifths is 12. One third of 30 is 10. Now take both groups away from 30.

solutions.reliable: One fifth of 30 is 6, so two fifths is 12 walkers. One third of 30 is 10 bus children. Together that is 22, so 30 - 22 = 8 children come by car. The transferable idea: turn each fraction into a number of children first, then subtract all the known groups from the whole.

whyOnTest: Fractions of a quantity are tested in two steps here, and each distractor stops after one step or misreads one fraction.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
